amanda: Heads-up - saw steady GPU memory growth (~30MB/min) on a Qwen-MQA long-context run (rope scale enabled) after ~12k tokens. Suspect KV fragmentation + kernel fallback.

diego: can you paste the runtime logs / kernel-selection trace?

amanda: here's the clipped trace from the run:
```
[2026-03-17T22:11:02Z] kernel.select -> prefer_fast (mqa-compatible)
[2026-03-17T22:11:02Z] kernel.fallback -> selected slow-kernel (seq>2048)
[2026-03-17T22:11:58Z] kv.alloc pages=8123 used=7981 free_frag=142 avg_page_frag=11.2
[2026-03-17T22:12:58Z] kv.alloc pages=8197 used=8040 free_frag=157 avg_page_frag=12.1
```

amanda: note the incremental page growth even with active eviction enabled.

sophia: interesting — when fallback to the slow kernel happens it changes paging stride and the allocator stops coalescing small frees efficiently. That matches the free_frag + rising avg_page_frag.

rebecca: repro script I used: `./perf_runner --model qwen-mqa --rope-scale 1.5 --seq 16384 --batch 1 --warmup 1k --request-rate 5/s`

rebecca: After ~40k tokens memory graph shows staircase growth, then small drops when prefix eviction happens but never fully compacts.

amanda: attaching the flame + kv histogram (pasted):
```
kv_free_buckets: [0:1245, 16:310, 32:98, 64:22, 128:6]
page_coalesces: 12
page_splits: 47
kernel_switch_count: 18
```

tim: could be MQA slot aliasing interacting with rope-scaling math. We saw similar but transient on Llama when seq crosses the GQA->MQA boundary. Qwen's token layout seems to produce more tiny leftover fragments.

diego: what about batching? are we doing any concat-batching that increases prefix reuse and prevents eviction?

amanda: test used continuous single requests, no batching. I did a run with batching=8 and saw slightly less page churn but still net growth.

sophia: two hypotheses: 1) kernel selection toggles per-request causing allocator fragmentation; 2) MQA/KV page mapping for qwen uses smaller slot size, so fragmentation amplifies under long rope rescaling. Both could be true.

rebecca: quick mitigations: increase `kv.compact_threshold` and run `kv.eager_coalesce=true` on the test host. That compacts pages periodically at cost of a short pause.

amanda: tried `kv.compact_threshold=0.25` -> saw compaction events but latency spikes (~120ms) at compaction. Not acceptable for SLAs.

tim: longer term we should make coalescing incremental and aware of kernel-selection epochs. If we treat a kernel switch as a barrier, avoid splitting pages across epochs.

diego: also worth looking at the kernel selection heuristics — why did it choose slow-kernel at seq>2048? maybe the cost model didn't account for MQA multi-slot overhead. If the model-specific cost table is off, server will oscillate.

amanda: I captured per-request `kernel_hash` and `kv.page_map` diff. There are repeated small allocations pinned to high-address slots that never get reused. Looks like a reuse miss pattern:
```
req 10234 -> pages [0x1a3..0x1b0]
req 10235 -> pages [0x1c0..0x1cf]
req 10236 -> pages [0x1a3..0x1b0] (reuse)
req 10237 -> pages [0x1d0..0x1df]
req 10238 -> pages [0x1e0..0x1ef]
```

amanda: reuse is intermittent, but coalesces rarely happen because small fragments are separated by live pages.

sophia: can you run with `--kv-page-size=64k` on Qwen to see if larger page grain reduces fragmentation? If yes, we should add model-specific page size heuristics for Qwen-MQA.

rebecca: scheduled a quick canary: `kv-page-size=64k` + `kv.eager_coalesce=false` on a dev host to measure long-run. I'll post graphs in an hour.

diego: another experiment: force the kernel to the fast path (override) for one run and see if the allocator stabilizes. If so, it proves kernel-switch churn is a multiplier.

amanda: I tried force-fast for 1h -> no memory growth, stable page map. So kernel toggling is a major factor.

tim: ok next steps: 1) short-term: add model-specific default `kv.page_size` for Qwen-MQA and a knob to bias kernel-selection cost model to avoid oscillation. 2) mid-term: allocator changes to do epoch-aware coalescing and incremental compaction. 3) long-term: add per-model kernel-cost calibration via small microbenchmarks on onboarding.

sophia: also add telemetry alert when `avg_page_frag > 10` AND `kernel_switch_count > 5` in a 5m window.

infra-bot: Created task RFC: #3456 "kv: epoch-aware coalescing + qwen-mqa page-size tweak" assigned to @sophia and @diego. ETA: triage meeting tomorrow 10:30 PT.

rebecca: noted. I'll post the canary results and heap dumps to the incident board.

amanda: thanks all — filing a perf regression ticket with logs + sample repro.

diego: great, thanks. feel free to ping me for bisect. :+1:
